title: Harmonize input composition: placeholders, autocompletion, and screen reader semantics
creator: Maya Patel
description: Audit and standardize interaction behaviors across text inputs, selects, and toggles with a focus on placeholders, browser/autocomplete hints, and screen reader semantics. The goal is consistent UX and improved accessibility across platforms and browsers while aligning with tokenized spacing and color roles.
background: Multiple teams reported inconsistent placeholder contrast, unexpected browser autofill visuals, and VoiceOver announcing redundant labels. These inconsistencies cause regressions in accessibility audits and visual flicker on autofill. Design tokens have evolved; some components still use legacy values.
goals: Create a single canonical approach for placeholder contrast and behavior
Define standard autocomplete attributes and recommended values per field type
Ensure screen readers announce inputs consistently (label, required state, hint)
Update component docs and tokens to reflect changes
Ship visual regressions tests and accessibility test cases
scope: Include text inputs, textarea, single-select, multi-select chips, toggles/switches, and the helper/hint/error row. Update tokens referenced by those components. Update React component props and docs. Provide migratory notes for existing consumers.
out_of_scope: Full redesign of form layout/grid, new field components (date-picker overhaul), backend validation logic.
acceptance_criteria: Placeholder text uses token 'text-muted-60' and passes 4.5:1 contrast with background when visible as hint
Autofill styling is neutralized across Chromium and Safari: no chrome-yellow or blue outlines; uses tokenized background 'surface-elevated-1'
Inputs announce: <label>, required status, and concise helper before accepting user input for VoiceOver and NVDA
Docs updated with code examples for autocomplete attributes (name, email, new-password, off) and a migration guide
Integration tests added to Storybook: visual snapshot for empty, focused, autofilled and error states on desktop and mobile viewport sizes
Design tokens updated and released in design-system-2026.04
tasks: Run a cross-browser audit: Chrome, Safari, Firefox, Edge (task assigned to Eng QA)
Update token palette mapping for placeholders and disabled text
Prototype keyboard and screen reader behavior with VoiceOver/NVDA and record short screencaps
Update React component prop 'autofill' recommendations and add 'autocomplete' presets in docs
Create Storybook stories for autofill and assistive technology scenarios
Work with Runtime/Frontend engineers to add CSS isolation for autofill pseudo-classes
proposed_design: Use explicit label prominence: label (token: label-regular) always visible; avoid relying on placeholders as primary labels
Placeholder treated as hint: lower contrast token and not announced as label by screen readers
Add a small helper API to components: aria-description-id -> helper row id, and ensure aria-describedby is set when helper exists
Provide recommended 'autocomplete' strings per semantic field in docs, including examples for complex forms (shipping vs billing)
implementation_notes: Front-end: update CSS variables for placeholder and autofill pseudo-classes; use -webkit-text-fill-color override for Chromium autofill backgrounds
Tokens: add 'text-placeholder' and 'autofill-bg' tokens and document usage
QA: capture accessibility snapshots with axe and manual VoiceOver test notes
Coordination: need Eng runtime to test impact on Dedicated/Private console screens where custom CSS overrides may apply
risks: Browser autofill hooks are inconsistent and sometimes locked to UA styles; CSS overrides can regress other inputs if not scoped
Changing placeholder contrast might affect visual density and perceived affordance; need stakeholder alignment
Third-party widgets embedded in customers' consoles may resist new CSS isolation approaches
